scope.purpose: Strengthen the six completed Sport Fagverk chapters with peer-reviewed academic research while preserving official rules, governance and facility sources as primary evidence for institutional facts.

principles: Official rules and institutional documents remain the best source for what a rule, policy, facility or governing body formally states.
Empirical, causal, health, learning, participation, identity and inequality claims require an academic research layer.
Every academic source is mapped to explicit existing claim IDs and carries an evidence class plus limitations.
Contradictory or methodologically contested literatures are represented rather than flattened into one certainty claim.
Cross-sectional associations are never rewritten as causal effects without stronger designs.

sources.title: Physical activity in relation to urban environments in 14 cities worldwide: a cross-sectional study
sources.limitations: Cross-sectional evidence supports environment-activity associations, not simple causal attribution to one facility.

sources.title: Sports mega-event legacies and adult physical activity: A systematic literature review and research agenda
sources.limitations: Mega-event evidence is heterogeneous and does not directly estimate everyday use of Oslo facilities.

sources.title: The impact of professional sports franchises and venues on local economies: A comprehensive survey
sources.limitations: Venue economics is context-dependent and cannot be generalized to social or health outcomes.

sources.title: Sport Mega-Events and Displacement of Host Community Residents: A Systematic Review
sources.journal: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
sources.limitations: Displacement evidence is concentrated on Olympic host contexts and cannot be transferred mechanically to local arena redevelopment.

sources.title: Performance analysis in football: a critical review and implications for future research
sources.limitations: Football-focused review; measurement and context findings should be transferred cautiously to other sports.

sources.title: Match analysis in football: a systematic review
sources.limitations: Evidence is football-specific and much of the underlying work is descriptive rather than causal.

sources.title: Unlocking the potential of big data to support tactical performance analysis in professional soccer: A systematic review
sources.limitations: Tracking-data findings depend on feature construction, aggregation and modelling choices; they are not raw ground truth.

sources.title: Match Analysis in Team Ball Sports: An Umbrella Review of Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses
sources.limitations: The umbrella review found low confidence in much of the underlying review literature, requiring cautious interpretation.

balance_requirements.reason: Represent both the earlier positive meta-analytic conclusion and the later publication-bias-sensitive reanalysis.

sources.title: How much is too much? (Part 1) International Olympic Committee consensus statement on load in sport and risk of injury
sources.limitations: Consensus synthesis is authoritative but not a single pooled causal estimate across all sports and athletes.

sources.title: Exercise-based injury prevention in child and adolescent sport: a systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.limitations: Evidence is strongest for organized youth sport and less complete for children under 14 and individual sports.

sources.title: Superiority of external attentional focus for motor performance and learning: Systematic reviews and meta-analyses
sources.limitations: Average effects span heterogeneous tasks and are explicitly balanced here against later publication-bias-sensitive reanalysis.

sources.title: Reporting bias, not external focus: A robust Bayesian meta-analysis and systematic review of the external focus of attention literature
sources.limitations: Reanalysis challenges a previously strong consensus and shows how publication bias can materially change conclusions.

sources.title: A systematic review of the psychological and social benefits of participation in sport for children and adolescents
sources.journal: International Journal of Behavioral Nutrition and Physical Activity
sources.limitations: Most included studies were cross-sectional, limiting causal conclusions about psychosocial benefits.

sources.title: Predictors of Persistent Participation in Youth Sport: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.limitations: Associations combine heterogeneous sports, measures and designs and do not prove one universal dropout mechanism.

sources.title: Motivations and Future Intentions in Sport Event Volunteering: A Systematic Review
sources.limitations: Focuses mainly on event volunteering, so transfer to routine club volunteering requires caution.

sources.title: Non-profit sports club volunteers: same, same, but different or one and the same?
sources.limitations: Survey evidence supports role heterogeneity but is not a universal causal model of volunteering.

sources.title: Is social identity theory enough to cover sports fans' behavior?: additional perspective from identity fusion theory
sources.limitations: Narrative review integrates identity frameworks; it is not a quantitative synthesis of effect sizes.

sources.title: Attending live sporting events predicts subjective wellbeing and reduces loneliness
sources.limitations: Observational UK survey associations have small effect sizes and do not establish that attendance causes wellbeing changes.

sources.title: Pathways to prejudice and outgroup hostility: Group alignment and intergroup conflict among football fans
sources.limitations: Fieldwork concerns specific supporter groups and should not be generalized to all fans or rivalries.

sources.title: Football Clubs as Identity Leaders: Communication and Club Action on Fan-Club Relationships
sources.journal: Journal of Community & Applied Social Psychology
sources.limitations: Qualitative sample is small and context-specific; it strengthens mechanism understanding rather than prevalence estimates.

sources.title: Fair play? Participation equity in organised sport and physical activity among children and adolescents in high income countries: a systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.journal: International Journal of Behavioral Nutrition and Physical Activity
sources.limitations: High-income-country evidence does not remove local variation in fees, welfare systems or sport structure.

sources.title: Barriers to and facilitators of sports participation for people with physical disabilities: a systematic review
sources.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
sources.limitations: Evidence overrepresents spinal cord injury and older studies; barrier patterns vary by impairment and age.

sources.title: A Systematic Review of Factors Associated with Sport Participation among Adolescent Females
sources.journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
sources.limitations: Focuses on adolescent girls and participation factors; it does not describe all gender identities or life stages.

sources.title: The impact of sports participation on psychological health and social outcomes in children and adolescents: a systematic review and update to the Mental Health through Sport conceptual model
sources.limitations: Observational evidence remains vulnerable to confounding even though the review also includes experimental and longitudinal studies.

sources.title: Does organized sports participation in childhood and adolescence positively influence health? A review of reviews
sources.limitations: A review of reviews inherits heterogeneity and quality limits from underlying syntheses and does not justify universal benefit claims.
